concepts.title: Random variable
concepts.definition: A function that associates a real number with each element in a sample space.
concepts.evidence: A random variable is a function that associates a real number with each element in the sample space.

concepts.title: Discrete sample space
concepts.definition: A sample space that contains a finite number of possibilities or an unending sequence with as many elements as there are whole numbers (countably infinite).
concepts.evidence: If a sample space contains a finite number of possibilities or an unending sequence with as many elements as there are whole numbers, it is called a discrete sample space.

concepts.title: Continuous sample space
concepts.definition: A sample space that contains an infinite number of possibilities equal to the number of points on a line segment.
concepts.evidence: If a sample space contains an infinite number of possibilities equal to the number of points on a line segment, it is called a continuous sample space.

concepts.title: Discrete random variable
concepts.definition: A random variable whose set of possible outcomes is countable.
concepts.evidence: A random variable is called a discrete random variable if its set of possible outcomes is countable.

concepts.title: Continuous random variable
concepts.definition: A random variable that can take on values on a continuous scale (such as an interval of real numbers).
concepts.evidence: When a random variable can take on values on a continuous scale, it is called a continuous random variable.

concepts.title: Probability mass function
concepts.definition: The set of ordered pairs $(x, f(x))$ representing the probability distribution of a discrete random variable $X$, satisfying: 1. $f(x) \ge 0$, 2. $\sum_x f(x) = 1$, and 3. $P(X = x) = f(x)$ for each possible outcome $x$.
concepts.evidence: The set of ordered pairs (x, f(x)) is a probability function, probability mass function, or probability distribution of the discrete random variable X
useWhen: Finding probabilities for individual values of a discrete random variable
Verifying whether a given discrete function qualifies as a valid probability distribution

concepts.title: Point probability of continuous random variables
concepts.definition: A continuous random variable has a probability of 0 of assuming exactly any single point value: $P(X = c) = 0$. Consequently, endpoint inclusion does not change interval probabilities: $P(a < X \le b) = P(a < X < b) = P(a \le X \le b) = P(a \le X < b)$.
concepts.evidence: A continuous random variable has a probability of 0 of assuming exactly any of its values. So, when X is continuous, P(a < X ≤ b) = P(a < X < b) + P(X = b) = P(a < X < b)
useWhen: Evaluating strict vs. non-strict inequality probabilities for continuous random variables

concepts.title: Probability density function
concepts.definition: A function $f(x)$ defined over the set of real numbers for a continuous random variable $X$ such that: 1. $f(x) \ge 0$ for all $x \in \mathbb{R}$, 2. $\int_{-\infty}^\infty f(x)\,dx = 1$, and 3. $P(a < X < b) = \int_a^b f(x)\,dx$.

concepts.title: Relationship between continuous CDF and PDF
concepts.definition: For a continuous random variable $X$ with cumulative distribution function $F(x)$ and probability density function $f(x)$, $P(a < X < b) = F(b) - F(a)$ and $f(x) = \frac{dF(x)}{dx}$ wherever the derivative exists.
